additional_context: Contrast case: SAME technology as primary, materially different organization and consequence environment. General creation-history findings must remain stable; organization-level implications must change.
adoption_posture: Conservative / risk-averse: no patient-facing autonomous behavior without extensive clinical validation and regulatory clearance
business_need: Emergency departments face intake bottlenecks; faster, consistent triage could reduce wait times, but errors directly endanger patients
capabilities_constraints: Has EHR infrastructure and clinical informatics staff; procurement requires HIPAA-compliant vendors; any AI use needs medical-legal review
emerging_technology: Agentic AI built on large language models (LLM-based agents that plan, use tools, and complete multi-step tasks)
intended_application: Patient intake triage support in a regional hospital emergency department: gathering symptoms, prioritizing cases for clinicians, drafting intake notes
management_question: Whether to allow any pilot of agentic AI in the intake workflow within the next 18 months
risk_consequence_context: Patient-safety-critical: a wrong triage suggestion can delay life-saving care; malpractice and regulatory exposure; errors are potentially irreversible
time_horizon: 18 months: decision on whether to permit a tightly supervised pilot
users_stakeholders: Patients, triage nurses, emergency physicians, hospital compliance and legal officers, EHR vendors
